title: Canonical morphism assignment for prescribed glueing objects
statement: Let R, S, φ, t and f be as in the canonical functor construction. Suppose obj assigns to every R-module M a formal glueing object with prime module S tensor_R M, charts M_(f i), and the actual canonical comparison and swap maps, as bundled-module equalities and heterogeneous map equalities in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. Then there exists a morphism assignment map, from every h : M → N to a Hom from obj M to obj N, preserving identities and composition, whose prime component is extendMap φ h and whose chart components are localMap (f i) h (by heterogeneous equality). No existence of obj is asserted, and no claim about an arbitrary pre-existing functor is made.

proof.text: Identify each restricted canonical chart with the localization as an R-module using Module.ext' and algebraMap_smul. Define the prime and chart maps by equality transport of extendMap and localMap. For prime compatibility, compare_properties gives invertibility of powers of the chart generator on the target. IsLocalizedModule.ext reduces to denominator-one fractions; the defining equation of exists_compare and tensor induction reduce both composites to the same pure tensor, using map_LocalizedModules. For chart compatibility, two fraction inductions and swap_properties give the same swapped fraction on both sides. Eliminate the supplied component equalities and heterogeneous structural-map equalities to transport these naturality equations to obj M and obj N. These components and equations construct a Hom for each h.

LinearMap.baseChange_id and baseChange_comp, together with IsLocalizedModule.map_id and map_comp', give the identity and composition laws for the canonical component maps. Equality elimination proves that transport preserves these component laws and yields the required heterogeneous equalities. Two Homs with equal prime and chart components are equal by structure cases and proof irrelevance, proving the functor laws.

proof_origin.place: Remark 05EL, construction of Can on morphisms; Algebra 07K0. Lean proof uses the existing canonical-map properties and defining comparison equation, localization extensionality, tensor induction, double fraction induction, and explicit equality transport.

mathlib_searches.results: CategoryTheory.Functor.of and Functorial package an already supplied morphism assignment and laws; no canonical formal glueing construction.
Functor, Functor.obj, Functor.map, identity and composition constructors. These do not establish the glueing object or morphism compatibility identities.

Mathlib has sheaf/topological glueing, not this formal glueing construction. Sheaf.Paper.FormalGlueingCanonicalMaps supplies fraction formulas, bijectivity and localized map laws. FormalGlueingData supplies the category and definitions. LinearMap.baseChange_id and baseChange_comp are in Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower. No duplicate of either intermediate theorem in lean/Sheaf or lean/WeilConjectures.

lean.statement:
theorem canonical_functor_maps {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (obj : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R → Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
      (obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
      (∀ i : Fin t, (obj M).M i =
        ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
      (∀ i j : Fin t,
        HEq ((obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))) :
    ∃ map : ∀ {M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R}, (M ⟶ N) → (obj M ⟶ obj N),
      (∀ M, map (𝟙 M) = 𝟙 (obj M)) ∧
      (∀ {M N P} (h : M ⟶ N) (k : N ⟶ P), map (h ≫ k) = map h ≫ map k) ∧
      (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom))
